2.3.1 GENERAL INTRODUCTION

Lichen is an organism consisting of a fungus and algae, so closely associated with each other as to appear a single organism. Hence, the lichen is a dual or composite organism. The fungal partner of lichen is known as mycobiont and the algal partner is known as phycobiont. In lichen thallus (body), the fungal partner cover maximum volume of the body and provide habitat, water, carbondioxide, shape and colour to the lichens while the algal partner produced food through photosynthesis which is utilized by both of them. The study of lichen is called lichenology. The father of lichenology is Theophrastus.
2.3.2 CHARACTERISTICS FEATURES OF LICHEN

Following are the characteristics features of lichen: 1. They are dual organisms having symbiotic association of algae and fungi. 2. Lichen grows usually in moist, cold and moderate temperature. They grow on barks of trees, leaves, dead logs, bare rocks etc. 3. The growth of lichen is very slow; they can survive for many years. 4. The body is thalloid, irregularly shaped and often deeply pigmented due to algal partner. On the basis of nature of thallus and their attachment to the substratum, lichens are crustose (closely attached and embedded to the substratum), foliose (flat leaf like) and fruticose (branched, shruby). 5. They are sensitive to air pollution and act as indicator of air pollution. 6. Lichen reproduces by vegetative, asexual and sexual method.
Examples: Graphis, Physcia, Usnea, etc.

2.3.3 ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE OF LICHEN
Lichens have both positive and negative effect as mentioned below:
Positive effects
1. Source of food: Lichens are the source of food for numerous minute organisms like mite, slugs, caterpillar etc. Certain species are also used by people for food.
2. Medical importance: Several lichens are used in the treatment of various diseases like Lobaria pulmonaria (in the treatment of lung disease), Xanthoria parientina (treatment of jaundice) etc.

3. Pioneers of ecological succession: Lichens are said to be the pioneers in establishing vegetation on bare rocky areas. They are the first members to colonize the barren rocky areas. They play an important role in nature in the formation of soil.

4. Bioindicator of air pollution: Lichens are very sensitive to atmospheric pollutants such as sulphur dioxide. As the level of air pollution increases, their number decreases. It helps to predict the level of air pollution.
5. Industry : Lichens are used to prepare different types of industrial products like dyes, cosmetics, perfumes, alcohol, litmus paper, etc.

Negative effect 1. Lichens growing on the walls of buildings can damage the plasters and shining beauty of buildings. 2. During dry season some species of lichens become so dry and inflammable that they catch fire and help in spreading forest fire.
